atoms.a: A river is a body of water that flows in one direction.
A lake is a large, fixed body of water that is surrounded by land.
A pond is a small, still body of water, often very shallow.

feedback.finish: Rivers, lakes and ponds are the three most common types of freshwater biome.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Rivers usually start in upland areas and continue until they reach another body of water, such as the ocean. The point where a river meets the sea is called an estuary.

As the river changes, so do the plants found along it. Plants that can handle strong currents, such mosses, grow in the upper course, and submerged or floating plants, such as water lilies, can be found further down as the current weakens.
Rivers are also home to lots of animals. They are especially important for salmon, who journey back from the sea to freshwater rivers to lay their eggs.

atoms.a: What types of plants are found in the upper course of a river?
Where would you find salmon eggs?

instruction.text: Find the crocodile to find out how it has adapted.

feedback.finish: Crocodiles are masters of camouflage and often live in the slightly salty waters of river estuaries. Saltwater crocodiles even have special salt glands that remove salt from their bodies!

instruction.text: Which types of water do you think contribute to the natural formation of lakes?

atoms.b: This satellite image shows the Great Lakes, which are a collective of deep, freshwater ((seas ++lakes)) that separate America and Canada.
They form the ((smallest ++largest)) surface area of fresh water in the world, covering an area greater than the United Kingdom!

atoms.a: Ponds are larger bodies of water than lakes.

feedback.wrong: Ponds are similar to lakes, but the biggest difference is that they are much smaller and shallower.

instruction.text: Drag the frog onto the lily pads to find out how it has adapted.

text: Frogs thrive in the wet, sheltered surroundings of a pond. Their webbed feet make them great swimmers and they are able to lay their frogspawn in the water.
